item.research_question: What is the mechanical behavior and resistance to shear localization of the single-phase fcc Al0.3CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy under high strain-rate dynamic loading?
item.processing_route: Vacuum-induction melting to cast a plate (~127 mm × 305 mm × 19 mm), followed by hot-isostatic-pressing (HIP) at 1,204 °C and 103 MPa for 4 hours, homogenization at 1,200 °C for 2 hours, and water quench.
item.test_conditions: Quasi-static compression (strain rate 10−4 s−1), dynamic compression using Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar (strain rates up to 1800 s−1 and 104 s−1), and forced shear localization using hat-shaped specimens at high strain rates.
key_findings: Yield stress increases from 216 MPa to 503 MPa as strain rate increases from 10−4 s−1 to 1.8 × 102 s−1.
Strain-rate sensitivity (m) is approximately 0.053, which is double that of coarse-grained pure aluminum (0.028).
The strain hardening rate of the alloy exceeds 1000 MPa, significantly higher than that of coarse-grained pure aluminum.
No adiabatic shear band was observed in hat-shaped samples subjected to an imposed shear strain of ~1.1.
At a strain rate of 104 s−1 and true strain of 0.5, the calculated temperature rise is only 109 K (to 402 K).
Mechanical twins with a ~36% area fraction and ~2.4 μm average thickness were observed in the deformed region.
Dynamic recrystallization was absent in the forced shear region, indicating the material continued to harden rather than soften.
item.mechanism: The authors propose that the combination of solid solution hardening, forest dislocation hardening, and mechanical twinning creates an excellent work hardening ability that suppresses shear localization. This high strain hardening ability, coupled with high strain-rate sensitivity and modest thermal softening, prevents the thermal softening from overcoming strain hardening, thereby inhibiting the formation of adiabatic shear bands.
item.limitations: The authors state that adiabatic shear localization of this alloy can only be activated by higher strains and temperatures than those imposed by their experiments.
quotes: The combination of multiple strengthening mechanisms such as solid solution hardening, forest dislocation hardening, as well as mechanical twinning leads to a high work hardening rate
However, no adiabatic shear band could be observed
The yield stress σy of the alloy increases from 216 MPa to 503 MPa when the strain rate increases from 10−4 s−1 to 1.8 × 102 s−1
